sufficiencyReasons: The definition's core structure (base of Consolidated Net Income plus addbacks minus subtractions) is fully represented. However, several complex conditions and provisos cannot be faithfully represented within the current node types:

Clause 1(d) contains a conditional mechanic (Borrower may elect not to add back non-cash charges that are accruals/reserves for future cash items, but if added back, the future cash payment must be subtracted) - this is a multi-period, choice-dependent reversal not expressible in the base IR

Clause 1(h) contains a complex reciprocal condition (add back only if non-cash gains relating to such income were deducted in Consolidated EBITDA in a prior period and not added back) - this references prior-period calculations and is not representable

Clause 1(l) contains pro forma run-rate calculations with a 12-month timeframe, good faith determinations, and incremental/non-duplicative conditions against Section 1.07(3) - while the cap is captured, the underlying calculation logic is unsupported
Clause 1(m) and the 10% cap basket condition requires understanding what qualifies as extraordinary/non-recurring/unusual which is subjective and fact-dependent
The reference to Section 1.07 for pro forma calculations (end of definition) means the actual computation methodology depends on that section's rules, which I have only partial visibility into
Multiple defined terms referenced (Permitted Acquisition, Borrower determination thresholds) could not be fully resolved within tool budget

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Represent a multi-period conditional addback/reversal mechanic: (1) Borrower may elect not to add back a non-cash charge in Period N if it represents an accrual/reserve for a future cash item, OR (2) if Borrower does add it back in Period N, then in Period N+X when the cash payment is made (excepting certain deferred compensation), the payment must be subtracted from Consolidated EBITDA. This is a choice-dependent, retroactive adjusting flow.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The current primitives (IF, SCHEDULE, DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE, ADD, SUBTRACT, etc.) cannot express a backward-looking condition that applies retroactively based on a prior-period choice. IF gates current-period logic; SCHEDULE handles stepped thresholds by future date but not retroactive adjustments. The semantic requires: 'check whether this charge was added in prior period, and if so, subtract the cash payment now' - this is a lookup into prior calculations and a contingent reversal, not a forward-looking condition.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: RETROACTIVE_ADJUSTMENT(priorPeriodReference, priorCondition, currentPeriodApplication) or a broader LOOKUP_AND_CONDITION primitive that can reference calculations in identified prior periods and apply contingent logic based on their outcomes. Alternatively, LEDGER_QUERY(itemType, periodRange, condition) to query whether a specific addback was used in a prior period.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Represent a reciprocal accrual/reversal mechanic: Add back cash receipts or netting arrangements in Period N only if (1) they do not represent Consolidated EBITDA or Consolidated Net Income in any prior period, AND (2) non-cash gains relating to such income were deducted in the calculation of Consolidated EBITDA in a prior period and have not been added back. This requires checking prior-period Consolidated EBITDA calculations for specific deductions and reversals.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The primitives cannot query or reference the content of prior-period Consolidated EBITDA calculations. METRIC_REFERENCE assumes a single metric value; it does not allow inspecting whether a specific component was included/excluded in a prior period's calculation of that metric. The logic is: 'IF (non-cash gain relating to this cash receipt was deducted in any prior Consolidated EBITDA) AND (such gain has not been added back since), THEN add back this cash receipt.' This is a dependency on prior-period calculation contents, not just on a metric's value.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: CALCULATION_HISTORY_CONDITION(metricName, periodRange, componentReference, condition) - a primitive that can query whether a specific adjustment was present in prior calculations of a metric and apply logic based on its presence/absence. Or a more general AUDIT_TRAIL_REFERENCE that allows checking whether a component was included in a prior calculation.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Represent 'run-rate' pro forma cost savings projections with good faith Borrower determination: The projected cost savings, synergies and operating expense reductions are stated as a 'run-rate' (full recurring benefit) calculated on a pro forma basis as though realized on the first day of the period, net of actual benefits realized during the period, subject to conditions that the actions are (a) reasonably identifiable and factually supportable, (b) undertaken or expected to be undertaken within 12 months, (c) non-duplicative of Section 1.07(3) adjustments, and (d) in aggregate capped at 15% of Acquired EBITDA. The calculation involves forward-looking projections with discretionary Borrower determination and a clawback for actual benefits realized.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The primitives can express the 15% cap (as a shared capacity) but cannot express: (1) the pro forma 'run-rate' calculation methodology (a full-year benefit even if partial-year implementation), (2) the good faith Borrower determination and the conditions of reasonableness/factual supportability (these are qualitative gating tests, not computable expressions), (3) the net-of-actual-benefits reversal in the same period, or (4) the incremental-but-not-duplicative relationship to Section 1.07(3). An IF or SCHEDULE primitive could gate on 'Permitted Acquisition occurred,' but the internal calculation (run-rate, netted against actuals, within 12 months of actions) is a complex, multi-variable projection logic.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: PRO_FORMA_PROJECTION(baseMetric, projectionLogic, realizationCheckpoint, realizationOffset, goodFaithCriteria) - a primitive that can encapsulate forward-looking pro forma calculations with internal netting logic and qualitative gating criteria. Alternatively, SYNERGY_ADDBACK(projectedAmount, realizationPeriod, realizationClawback, duplicativeTestReference) - more narrowly scoped to the synergy/cost-savings use case.

sufficiencyReasons: The definition's core structure (base of Consolidated Net Income plus addbacks minus subtractions) is fully represented. However, several complex conditions and provisos cannot be faithfully represented within the current node types:

Clause 1(d) contains a conditional mechanic (Borrower may elect not to add back non-cash charges that are accruals/reserves for future cash items, but if added back, the future cash payment must be subtracted) - this is a multi-period, choice-dependent reversal not expressible in the base IR

Clause 1(h) contains a complex reciprocal condition (add back only if non-cash gains relating to such income were deducted in Consolidated EBITDA in a prior period and not added back) - this references prior-period calculations and is not representable

Clause 1(l) contains pro forma run-rate calculations with a 12-month timeframe, good faith determinations, and incremental/non-duplicative conditions against Section 1.07(3) - while the cap is captured, the underlying calculation logic is unsupported
Clause 1(m) and the 10% cap basket condition requires understanding what qualifies as extraordinary/non-recurring/unusual which is subjective and fact-dependent
The reference to Section 1.07 for pro forma calculations (end of definition) means the actual computation methodology depends on that section's rules, which I have only partial visibility into
Multiple defined terms referenced (Permitted Acquisition, Borrower determination thresholds) could not be fully resolved within tool budget

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Represent a multi-period conditional addback/reversal mechanic: (1) Borrower may elect not to add back a non-cash charge in Period N if it represents an accrual/reserve for a future cash item, OR (2) if Borrower does add it back in Period N, then in Period N+X when the cash payment is made (excepting certain deferred compensation), the payment must be subtracted from Consolidated EBITDA. This is a choice-dependent, retroactive adjusting flow.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The current primitives (IF, SCHEDULE, DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE, ADD, SUBTRACT, etc.) cannot express a backward-looking condition that applies retroactively based on a prior-period choice. IF gates current-period logic; SCHEDULE handles stepped thresholds by future date but not retroactive adjustments. The semantic requires: 'check whether this charge was added in prior period, and if so, subtract the cash payment now' - this is a lookup into prior calculations and a contingent reversal, not a forward-looking condition.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: RETROACTIVE_ADJUSTMENT(priorPeriodReference, priorCondition, currentPeriodApplication) or a broader LOOKUP_AND_CONDITION primitive that can reference calculations in identified prior periods and apply contingent logic based on their outcomes. Alternatively, LEDGER_QUERY(itemType, periodRange, condition) to query whether a specific addback was used in a prior period.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Represent a reciprocal accrual/reversal mechanic: Add back cash receipts or netting arrangements in Period N only if (1) they do not represent Consolidated EBITDA or Consolidated Net Income in any prior period, AND (2) non-cash gains relating to such income were deducted in the calculation of Consolidated EBITDA in a prior period and have not been added back. This requires checking prior-period Consolidated EBITDA calculations for specific deductions and reversals.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The primitives cannot query or reference the content of prior-period Consolidated EBITDA calculations. METRIC_REFERENCE assumes a single metric value; it does not allow inspecting whether a specific component was included/excluded in a prior period's calculation of that metric. The logic is: 'IF (non-cash gain relating to this cash receipt was deducted in any prior Consolidated EBITDA) AND (such gain has not been added back since), THEN add back this cash receipt.' This is a dependency on prior-period calculation contents, not just on a metric's value.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: CALCULATION_HISTORY_CONDITION(metricName, periodRange, componentReference, condition) - a primitive that can query whether a specific adjustment was present in prior calculations of a metric and apply logic based on its presence/absence. Or a more general AUDIT_TRAIL_REFERENCE that allows checking whether a component was included in a prior calculation.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Represent 'run-rate' pro forma cost savings projections with good faith Borrower determination: The projected cost savings, synergies and operating expense reductions are stated as a 'run-rate' (full recurring benefit) calculated on a pro forma basis as though realized on the first day of the period, net of actual benefits realized during the period, subject to conditions that the actions are (a) reasonably identifiable and factually supportable, (b) undertaken or expected to be undertaken within 12 months, (c) non-duplicative of Section 1.07(3) adjustments, and (d) in aggregate capped at 15% of Acquired EBITDA. The calculation involves forward-looking projections with discretionary Borrower determination and a clawback for actual benefits realized.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The primitives can express the 15% cap (as a shared capacity) but cannot express: (1) the pro forma 'run-rate' calculation methodology (a full-year benefit even if partial-year implementation), (2) the good faith Borrower determination and the conditions of reasonableness/factual supportability (these are qualitative gating tests, not computable expressions), (3) the net-of-actual-benefits reversal in the same period, or (4) the incremental-but-not-duplicative relationship to Section 1.07(3). An IF or SCHEDULE primitive could gate on 'Permitted Acquisition occurred,' but the internal calculation (run-rate, netted against actuals, within 12 months of actions) is a complex, multi-variable projection logic.

findings.verifierReasoning: The source text explicitly states a joint capacity constraint ('provided that the aggregate amount of any amounts added back to Consolidated EBITDA pursuant to clauses (f), (m) and (n) above shall not exceed 10% of Consolidated EBITDA'). This is a material, independently operative limitation that restricts what can be added back in any Test Period. The proposed IR represents each of these items as separate additive components with no cap or grouping constraint shown. A borrower relying on the IR alone would not know that the combined total of these three categories must be limited to 10% of unadjusted Consolidated EBITDA. This is a real economic difference—whether these three items can be added in full or only to the extent their sum does not exceed 10% is a material constraint on the definition.
